section_summary: This section continues a translated account of Japanese fisheries education, then reproduces regulations governing the Fisheries Institute and fisheries experimental stations, including their courses, admissions, staffing and research work. Correspondence in 1940 discusses the value of the report for U.S. fisheries training. The final pages introduce a memorandum on Japan’s whaling industry.

subfiles.title: Fisheries school curricula and regulations, continuation
subfiles.about: Completes curriculum tables and regulations for a Japanese fisheries school.
subfiles.summary: The remaining tables describe the piscicultural curriculum and laboratory work, followed by rules for research and elective students. Supplementary provisions address the transition from the former fisheries course attached to Hokkaido Imperial University.

subfiles.title: Ministerial Regulations for the Fisheries Institute
subfiles.about: Prescribes the Institute’s courses, admission qualifications and extensive curricula.
subfiles.summary: The ordinance establishes regular, postgraduate and pelagic fisheries courses and sets admission qualifications and periods of study. Detailed tables cover fishing, manufacturing and piscicultural instruction, including laboratory, vessel and field practice. Later provisions govern elective students and special courses; the text incorporates amendments through April 1937.

subfiles.title: Institute Regulations for the Fisheries Institute
subfiles.about: Sets detailed rules for admission, study, fees and graduation across the Institute’s courses.
subfiles.summary: These revised regulations define the school calendar, entrance examinations, student residence and discipline, examinations, graduation and tuition. Separate chapters govern the graduate and pelagic fisheries courses and elective students. The pelagic course includes eligibility restrictions, naval training and practice outside the Institute.

subfiles.title: Organization of the Fisheries Institute
subfiles.about: Defines the Institute’s supervision, staff and official duties.
subfiles.summary: The ordinance places the Institute under the Minister of Agriculture and Forestry and specifies its staff and their duties.

subfiles.title: Regulations for the Conduct of Business of the Fisheries Institute
subfiles.about: Allocates educational and administrative work within the Institute.
subfiles.summary: The regulations assign responsibilities to instruction and general affairs departments and require ministerial approval or reporting for specified rules and results.

subfiles.title: Special Regulations for the Admission of Foreigners to the Fisheries Institute
subfiles.about: Sets application, examination and certification rules for foreign students.
subfiles.summary: Foreign applicants must supply an introduction from a diplomatic office and undergo the Institute’s examinations. The regulations specify how admitted students may be promoted and certified.

subfiles.title: Regulations for Prefectural Fisheries Experimental Stations
subfiles.about: Governs the establishment, work and reporting of prefectural fisheries experimental stations.
subfiles.summary: The regulations limit each prefecture to one station, allow branches and prescribe staff, research and public services. Governors must obtain permission to establish or abolish stations and submit annual reports. The text records later amendments.

subfiles.title: Organization of the Fisheries Experimental Station
subfiles.about: Defines the national station’s functions, staffing and branch authority.
subfiles.summary: The ordinance establishes the station’s research, analytical, distribution and teaching functions under the Minister of Agriculture and Forestry.

subfiles.title: Regulations for the Conduct of Business of the Fisheries Experimental Station
subfiles.about: Assigns scientific and administrative duties among the station’s departments and branches.
subfiles.summary: Three research departments cover fishing and manufacture, biological and physical research, and oceanography. A general affairs department handles records, staff and accounts; the director oversees branches and reports results.

subfiles.title: Regulations for Experiments by the Fisheries Experimental Station
subfiles.about: Sets application and sample rules for experiments, analyses, inspections and expert opinions.
subfiles.summary: A detailed schedule specifies sample quantities for aquatic foods, oils, fishing equipment and other materials. The regulations also address refusal of applications, return of samples and applicant expenses, transferring pending work from the Fisheries Institute.

subfiles.title: Application for Experiment, Analysis, Inspection or Expert Opinion
subfiles.to: Director of the Fisheries Experimental Station
subfiles.about: Provides fields for a requested service, supporting documents and samples.
subfiles.summary: Blank form for an applicant’s request, sample details, address, name and seal.

subfiles.title: Regulations for the Sale of Seedlings by the Fisheries Experimental Station
subfiles.about: Governs the sale or free distribution of aquatic plant and animal seedlings.
subfiles.summary: The regulations define eligible recipients, applications, payment, delivery and subsequent reporting. Seedlings may be supplied without cost for approved cultivation experiments.

subfiles.title: Regulations for Students of the Fisheries Experimental Station
subfiles.to: Fisheries Experimental Station and prospective students
subfiles.about: Sets qualifications, applications and terms for practical training at the station.
subfiles.summary: The notice limits training to two years, establishes eligibility and application requirements, and places student expenses on students. Attached blank forms provide an application and a pledge signed by a guarantor.

subfiles.title: Moore’s forwarding letter on Japanese fisheries training
subfiles.about: Forwards the Tokyo consulate’s report on training personnel for Japanese fisheries.
subfiles.summary: Moore highlights the report’s account of numerous schools and experimental stations.

subfiles.title: Department of State commendation of Richardson’s report
subfiles.from: Breckinridge Long, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Commends the consulate’s report on Japanese fisheries training.
subfiles.summary: The Department rates W. Garland Richardson’s March 6 report “EXCELLENT” and asks that he be informed.

subfiles.title: Ickes’s response to the Japanese fisheries training report
subfiles.about: Compares Japanese fisheries training and research capacity with that of the United States.
subfiles.summary: Ickes thanks Moore for the report and describes U.S. shortages of fisheries schools and research vessels. He discusses a trawler conversion, the Bristol Bay salmon investigation and the need for a West Coast research vessel, then requests further fisheries information.

subfiles.title: Moore’s reply to Ickes
subfiles.about: Offers State Department cooperation on fisheries training and conservation.
subfiles.summary: Moore agrees on the importance of trained personnel and promises active State Department cooperation.

subfiles.title: Cover memorandum on the Japanese whaling industry
subfiles.about: Introduces a memorandum condensed from a Japan Times and Mail fisheries supplement.
subfiles.summary: Notes uncertain verification while describing Japan’s growing fleet and efforts to use more whale products.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on Japanese Whaling Industry
subfiles.about: Begins an account of Japanese Antarctic whaling catches and fleet development.
subfiles.summary: Reports the 1938–39 catch, oil output and fleet size, and traces Japanese Antarctic whaling to 1934; the memorandum continues beyond this section.
